title: Fulfillments
description: Track shipments and delivery of product orders.

help.title: About Fulfillments
help.overview: A fulfillment is one shipment of a product order. Shipping an order creates one. You can also create one here. Its status is pending, shipped, delivered, or failed, and that status feeds the order.

sections.title: How a shipment moves
sections.body: Ship, deliver, and fail are only legal from the status named here. The order itself has to be ready too.
items: Ship is only from pending, and only when the order is not still pending, cancelled, or refunded.
Shipping consumes the stock reserved for those lines and can move the order to shipped.
Deliver is only from shipped. Delivering the last open shipment can move the order to delivered.
Fail is from pending or shipped. Failing a shipment that already left reverses that shipment. If the order is cancelled or refunded, stock still held is released.

sections.title: What you record on it
sections.body: The shipment is the place for the carrier and the tracking, not the order header.
items: Carrier, tracking number, and tracking link are the details the customer is told when it ships.
Shipped at, estimated delivery, and delivered at mark the timeline.
The lines are quantities of the order's items. A later shipment can cover what an earlier one left.

sections.title: How it sits with the order
sections.body: The order's fulfillment status is derived from its shipments, so a partial ship leaves the order partly fulfilled.
items: Open the order from the row when you need payment, cancel, or refund. Those stay on the order.
A return that is received puts goods back in the warehouse the line shipped from.
Deleting a fulfillment is a soft delete and it can be restored.
